facts.raw_span: A 59-year-old woman presented with a lump in the lower outer quadrant of her left breast
Six years earlier, she had undergone breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) to the left breast for an upper inner quadrant carcinoma
there was a 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
the overlying skin was uninvolved
there were no palpable axillary lymph nodes
Mammography showed a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealed a lobulated, well-defined mass measuring 17.5 × 16.4 × 10.6 mm with relatively hypoechoic, heterogeneous internal echoes
A core-needle biopsy of the lesion suggested only atrophic mammary glands
On three-month follow-up, the lesion had increased in size

concepts.why: The patient has a history of radiation therapy to the left breast and now presents with a growing mass in the same area, which is consistent with postradiation sarcoma.
The patient has a history of breast cancer and now presents with a new mass in the same breast, which could be a recurrence of the original cancer.
The patient has a history of radiation therapy to the left breast and now presents with a mass in the same area, which could be consistent with radiation-induced fibrosis.
The patient presents with a mass in the breast, which could be a benign tumor such as a fibroadenoma or breast cyst.

rationales.F02: History of radiation therapy increases the risk of postradiation sarcoma and radiation-induced fibrosis.
rationales.F03: A firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle is concerning for a malignant tumor such as postradiation sarcoma or recurrent breast cancer.
rationales.F07: The ultrasonography findings of a lobulated, well-defined mass with heterogeneous internal echoes are suspicious for a malignant tumor.
rationales.F08: The core-needle biopsy suggesting atrophic mammary glands does not support a diagnosis of a malignant tumor, but rather suggests a benign or inflammatory process.
rationales.F09: The increase in size of the lesion on follow-up is concerning for a malignant tumor such as postradiation sarcoma or recurrent breast cancer.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of radiation therapy and the presence of a new, growing mass in the irradiated field, along with the ultrasonography findings, support postradiation sarcoma as the most likely diagnosis.
